transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I, um… I came in because I haven’t really been sleeping. Since that warehouse inspection, I just lie there replaying parts of it, and if I do fall asleep I wake up sweating… like I’m back near the blast.
During the day, do you find yourself having sudden, vivid memories of the warehouse inspection that feel like you’re reliving it?

Yeah… sometimes. I’ll be at work, like reviewing a policy or a loss report, and then I suddenly see it again—just this flash of the worker on the floor, the soot in the air. It’s not like I’m trying to think about it. My body just reacts before I can really stop it.
Have you been avoiding certain places, people, or activities that remind you of the warehouse inspection?
Yeah… a bit. I’ve been avoiding the warehouse file. And when calls come in about industrial accounts, I sometimes just let them go to voicemail. Even opening those emails makes my stomach drop.
Since the warehouse inspection, have you been feeling ongoing fear, anger, or guilt that seems tied to what happened there?
I don’t know… not really in a way I can name. I’m unsettled, I guess, but I haven’t really sorted out if it’s fear or guilt or anything like that.

Since the warehouse inspection, have you noticed that you feel a persistent sense of fear, anger, or guilt that seems directly related to what happened there? For example, do you feel on edge, overly responsible, or unable to let go of the event emotionally?
I… I don’t think so. I mean, I’m tense about it, but I wouldn’t say there’s one feeling like fear or guilt that just stays there all the time. It’s more… I don’t know. Hard to pin down.
Since the warehouse inspection, have you had any ongoing emotional reactions like feeling fearful, guilty, or angry specifically about what happened there?
Not really… I mean, I’ve felt off since then, but I don’t know that I’d call it fear or guilt or anger about it. It’s just… hard to explain.
Since the warehouse inspection, have you noticed yourself feeling emotionally numb, detached, or having a reduced ability to experience positive emotions like joy or love?
I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say numb exactly… I just haven’t really been paying attention to that. I don’t think I’ve noticed anything like that clearly.
Since the warehouse inspection, have you had a lasting emotional reaction, like feeling afraid, guilty, or angry specifically about what happened there, even if it's not constant?
I don’t think so. Not in a clear way, anyway. I get unsettled when I think about it, but I wouldn’t say there’s some lasting fear or guilt or anger that I can point to.
Since the warehouse inspection, have you noticed any ongoing changes in your mood, like feeling more irritable, distant from others, or unable to enjoy things you used to?

Maybe irritable, yeah. I… snapped at a junior analyst over some small spreadsheet question. It came out way harsher than I meant, and I felt pretty embarrassed after. I’m not usually like that with people.
Since the warehouse inspection, have you had any persistent feelings, like fear, anger, or guilt, that you can clearly link back to what happened there?
Not really. I mean, I don’t feel good about it, but I can’t clearly say it’s fear or guilt or anger that’s been sticking around.

Since the warehouse inspection, have you had any persistent emotional state, even if it comes and goes, that you can clearly link back to the event—like feeling afraid, guilty, or angry when thinking about it?
I don’t think I can clearly link a feeling like that to it. I get uncomfortable when it comes up, but… I wouldn’t call it fear or guilt or anger exactly.
Since the warehouse inspection, have you had any ongoing emotional reactions—like feeling fearful, guilty, or angry—specifically when thinking about what happened there?
I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t like thinking about it, but I wouldn’t say I get clearly fearful or guilty or angry. It’s more just… uncomfortable, I guess.
Since the warehouse inspection, have you noticed yourself feeling unusually anxious, down, or emotionally reactive in general, even when you're not thinking about the event?
I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed anything like that in general… maybe I’m a little on edge sometimes, but I can’t say it’s unusual or connected.
Since the warehouse inspection, have you noticed yourself being more easily startled, on edge, or unusually reactive to things that wouldn’t have bothered you before?
Yeah… I guess so. Like if a printer jams or a door slams, I jump more than I should. Even someone coming up behind my desk can make me really tense, and it takes me a few minutes to calm down.

Since the warehouse inspection, have you had any persistent emotional state — even if it comes and goes — that you can clearly link back to the event, such as feeling afraid, guilty, or angry specifically about what happened there?
Not really. I mean, I can tell it bothers me, but I can’t say I’m walking around feeling afraid or guilty or angry about it specifically. It’s more vague than that.
Since the warehouse inspection, have you had any persistent negative emotional state, such as feeling fearful, guilty, angry, or sad, that you can clearly link back to what happened there?
I don’t think so. I mean, it’s been bothering me, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been stuck in fear or guilt or anger about it. Not in a clear way.
